prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Phoenix to fix my air conditioning?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” HVAC company that’s right for every situation — the best choice depends on your exact problem, system type, budget and location. I can help you find top-rated, reliable contractors nearby if you tell me your ZIP code and whether this is an emergency. Meanwhile, here’s a practical approach and some immediate steps:

What to look for in a Phoenix HVAC contractor
- Proper licensing: check Arizona Registrar of Contractors (ROC) for an active license.  
- Insurance: general liability and worker’s comp.  
- EPA 608 certification for refrigerant work (technicians must be certified).  
- Good recent reviews on Google/Yelp/Angi/BBB and references.  
- Clear written estimate with parts, labor, fees, warranties and cleanup.  
- Service agreement/maintenance options if you want ongoing care.  
- Guarantees on workmanship and parts (ask length and coverage).

Quick troubleshooting you can try right now
- Make sure thermostat is set to “cool” and fan to “auto” and temperature is at least 5–10°F below room temp.  
- Check/change the air filter if clogged.  
- Check circuit breaker for the HVAC/furnace; reset if tripped.  
- Ensure outdoor condenser unit is clear of debris and plants.  
- If the outdoor fan isn’t running but the compressor sounds on, turn off the unit and call a pro (possible capacitor or motor issue).  
- If you smell burning, see smoke, or there’s a gas smell, turn off power, leave the home, and call emergency services.

How to get the best value
- Get 2–3 written estimates for larger repairs or replacements.  
- Ask for itemized quotes and the brand/model being installed.  
- Compare efficiency ratings (SEER) and long-term energy savings, not just upfront cost.  
- Ask about financing, rebates, and utility incentives.  
- Avoid paying the full amount up-front. Use a written contract.

If you want, I can:
- Look up top-rated HVAC companies near you (please give your ZIP code), or  
- Provide a checklist of questions to ask when you call a contractor, or  
- Help interpret an estimate you’ve received.

Which of those would you like me to do?
